analysis:
In a Rajya Sabha reply in September 2011, Jairam Ramesh reported rural sanitation coverage of about 73 per cent as of July 2011, up from 21.9 per cent in Census 2001. The figure came from the Total Sanitation Campaign's administrative progress reports.

Census 2011 counted 32.7 per cent of rural households with a latrine within their premises. In a later Lok Sabha reply, the same minister cited the Census figure of 32.7 per cent, a much lower measure of household access.

The 73 per cent figure therefore measures toilets constructed or reported under the programme, not the share of rural households with a working latrine; presented as sanitation coverage without that qualification, it is misleading.
